title: Reading the price board
summary: Prices in TCG Card Shop Simulator are shown, not hidden: the game draws item prices as their own lines in the interface and gives checking a price its own screen.
body: Price information is presented as lines you read rather than a number you have to remember, which is why the game groups them together.
Checking a price is a deliberate action with its own screen, so you can look something up before you commit to a tag.
Because tags on the floor are objects too, what the board says and what the shelf says are two views of the same decision.
What this entry does not tell you: how often prices move or which lines matter most. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Item prices are drawn as grouped lines in the interface.
Checking a price has its own screen.
Price tags on the floor are separate objects.
The price screen pages through cards, with a panel list, highlighted page buttons, a card page option group and an expansion text.
That paging scrolls between a start and an end offset, stops at a scroll-end parent, and caps how many card elements a page may hold.
The price screen carries the same three colours as the price graph: a positive, a negative and a neutral one.
The build ships one sheet holding the tag artwork itself: the numerals, the separators and the currency signs the tags are written with.
